slides.title: HFLD Readiness Training
slides.text:
- Learning Objectives
- Process reference data collected
- Understand the process and inputs needed for analysis
- Conduct accuracy assessment and area adjustment

slides.title: HFLD Readiness Training
slides.text:
- Why can’t we use land cover maps as they are?
- Classification errors
- No indication of over/under-estimation
- No uncertainty of estimates
- Objectives of Sampling
- Estimate areas with characteristics we want in an unbiased manner
- Assess the accuracy of a land cover map
- Derive the uncertainty of our estimation

slides.title: HFLD Readiness Training
slides.text:
- Objectives of Validation
- Assess the accuracy of a land cover map
- Derive the uncertainty of our estimation
- Additional Objectives if required
- Use our uncertainty to adjust our initial estimate
- ART-TREES typically requires forest cover maps to have accuracy > 90%
- Verra Avoided Unplanned Deforestation requires forest cover maps to have uncertainty < 20%
- AND
- Use uncertainty to adjust deforestation estimates

slides.title: HFLD Readiness Training
slides.text:
**Note:** in Landis and Koch's scale, 0.81–1.0 is "almost perfect" agreement; Olofsson et al. (2014) advise against relying on kappa.

- Confusion Matrix
- Vertical Axis: What was the sample classified as?
- Horizontal Axis: What land cover is the sample in reality?
- Results:
- User’s Accuracy: Errors of Commission
  - How wrong is the classification?
- Producer’s Accuracy: Errors of Omission
  - How much did the classification miss?
- Overall Accuracy
- Kappa Coefficient

| Kappa value | Strength of agreement |
|---|---|
| < 0 | Poor agreement |
| 0–0.20 | Slight agreement |
| 0.21–0.40 | Fair agreement |
| 0.41–0.60 | Moderate agreement |
| 0.61–0.80 | Substantial agreement |
| 0.81–1.0 | Perfect agreement |

slides.title: HFLD Readiness Training
slides.text:
- Unbiased Sample-based Area Adjustment
- Using User Accuracy of each class
- Adjust our initial area estimate
- Example
- With a initial forest estimate of 2,700,000 hectares, 70% forest cover
- Out of 100 Classified Forest Points
- 98 points are Forest
- 98% User Accuracy
- Our adjusted forest estimate is 98% x 70 = 68.6% forest cover
- Our adjusted forest area is 2,646	,000 hectares

slides.title: HFLD Readiness Training
slides.text:
**Correction:** the standard error in this example is 1,495 ha, not 1,435 ha (1.6449 × 1,495 = 2,459).

- Percentage Uncertainty
- Half-width of 90% Confidence Interval of estimate
- As a proportion of the estimate
- Example
- Initial estimate of 17,000 hectares of deforestation
- 18/23 classified samples are actually deforestation
- Our adjusted deforestation area is 13,304 hectares
- We calculate the standard error is 1,435 hectares
- We are 90% sure the real deforestation area is ±2,459 of 13,304 hectares
- We are therefore 18.5% uncertain about our estimate
